transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?
I'm really struggling because I feel so unhappy and distressed about my skin. I have these terrible acne breakouts and scars all over my face, and it makes me feel incredibly self-conscious.
How much time each day do you spend thinking about your skin, checking it, or trying to hide it?

Honestly, I spend several hours every single day obsessing over how my skin looks and constantly checking it in the mirror. It also takes me a really long time to try and camouflage all the flaws with heavy makeup before I can even feel okay enough to go outside.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, Adjustment Disorder]. Based on the interview, the patient has intense preoccupation with perceived skin flaws, spends several hours daily checking and camouflaging them, and experiences significant distress and impairment—this strongly supports Body Dysmorphic Disorder. Major Depressive Disorder and Adjustment Disorder are less likely because the symptoms described are specifically centered on appearance-related preoccupation rather than a broader depressive syndrome or a clear stressor-related adjustment reaction.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has intense preoccupation with perceived facial skin defects (acne/scarring), spends several hours daily thinking about and checking the skin, and uses heavy camouflage to hide it, causing marked distress and impairment. This pattern is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder rather than a primary obsessive-compulsive disorder.
